title: PiSPICE: Accelerating Post-Layout SPICE Simulation via Essential Parasitic Identification
problem: Post-layout SPICE simulation of advanced-node ICs involves billions to trillions of parasitic nodes, creating prohibitively high computational cost that slows design closure and verification cycles.
motivation: As feature sizes shrink and integration increases, post-layout simulations dominate design cycles, but directly analyzing billions of parasitic elements becomes computationally intractable, demanding smarter reduction approaches.
method: PiSPICE uses adjoint sensitivity analysis (a mathematical technique for finding which components affect results) on pre-layout circuits (before physical layout) to identify critical parasitic elements (unwanted electrical components that appear in densely packed circuits). Only these critical parasitics are kept in the post-layout simulation; model order reduction (a technique that simplifies their representation) minimizes their computational impact while non-critical parasitics are removed entirely. This reduces simulation scale from billions or trillions of nodes to just the essential ones.
key_novelty: PiSPICE is the first to use adjoint sensitivity analysis (a technique that finds which components affect results) on pre-layout circuits to identify essential parasitic elements (unwanted circuit components), avoiding expensive analysis of billion-node post-layout circuits and achieving 17.27x speedup.
contributions: Adjoint sensitivity analysis method for identifying critical parasitics on pre-layout circuits.
Model order reduction for non-critical parasitic impact minimization.
17.27x simulation speedup with <0.78% error vs commercial simulator Spectre.
primary_theme: post-layout SPICE acceleration via parasitic identification
